newsitem.title: USA: IRS extends deadline on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: IRS extends deadline on yield burning.

text.p: The Internal Revenue Service said Wednesday it is extending the deadline for requesting a closing agreement under its controversial July ruling on yield burning.
"This notice requests comments on Revenue Procedure 96-41 and modifies Section 5.01 by extending the deadline for requesting a closing agreement under the program," IRS said in a five-page notice.
The IRS said it is extending the deadline from July 19 to at least one year from the date it publishes further guidance. IRS did not say when it will publish further guidance.
"In the meantime, issuers can continue to take advantage of the closing agreement program," the IRS said. IRS requested comments by December 17.
IRS invited comments on what is an appropriate time period within which to request a closing agreement under Revenue Procedure 96-41.
"What methods or procedures are appropriate to determine spot price (including the range of values acceptable as spot price) for purposes of determining the closing agreement amount?" IRS said.
"Are there other methods appropriate for determining closing agreement amount that would be easier for the service and issuers to apply?" IRS said.

IRS asked whether alternative closing agreement programs are warranted for all types of issues or for particular types of issues, such as small offerings, bonds issued before August 15, 1986 or prior to other effective dates of the Tax Reform Act of 1986.
The IRS said the spot price of any particular bond did not necessarily reflect its fair value.
